claims.text: Graceful degradation: when a dependency fails, the system keeps its most important functions and loses only what needs that dependency, in a way chosen in advance.

Program.cs @ stage-2 lines 75-80 registers one health check, AddDbContextCheck<DonHangDbContext>(tags: ["ready"]); the comment says Redis is left out on purpose. Lines 123-124 map /health/ready to run only checks tagged "ready". No mail server check exists.
The DbContext health check (AddDbContextCheck) by default calls EF Core's CanConnectAsync, so it fails when the database cannot be reached.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: 'Health checks in ASP.NET Core', section 'Entity Framework Core DbContext probe'

claims.text: With default HealthCheckOptions, a health endpoint answers 200 when the report is Healthy and 503 when it is Unhealthy.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: 'Health checks in ASP.NET Core', 'Customize the HTTP status code' (ResultStatusCodes defaults)

claims.text: A Pod whose readiness probe fails is removed from the endpoints of the Services that select it, so it gets no requests through them; a failing readiness probe restarts nothing.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: 'Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes' / 'Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes'; deploy/k8s/api.yaml @ stage-2 lines 38-52

claims.text: ProductCache.GetAsync (ProductCache.cs @ stage-2 lines 61-76) catches only RedisException or RedisTimeoutException via an exception filter, logs a warning and returns null; other exceptions propagate.

FindAsync (ProductCache.cs @ stage-2 L25-49) treats a null from GetAsync as a miss, tries GetAsync again under its per-key lock, then calls inner.FindAsync (one query). Only GET /api/v1/products/{id} uses it; the list reads DonHangDbContext directly.
The Redis connection string at stage-2 sets abortConnect=false, and ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs sets options.BacklogPolicy = BacklogPolicy.FailFast.
QueuedNotifier.Send (QueuedNotifier.cs @ stage-2 lines 9-23) only adds a Notification with Status "pending" to the order's DbContext; it does not contact the mail server.
Captured output of email-retry.sh @ stage-2 (Mailpit stopped): the order POST answers 201; the email row fails attempts 1-5 and ends 'failed | 5 | t'.
NotificationSender marks a row failed after its fifth failed attempt (MaxAttempts = 5) and never picks it up again; the five attempts span about 40 s in all, so a longer mail outage loses the email.

claims.text: deploy/k8s @ stage-2: api.yaml runs 2 api replicas with readinessProbe on /health/ready; redis.yaml runs one Redis replica shared by them (redis:6379).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: deploy/k8s/api.yaml lines 11, 38-52; deploy/k8s/redis.yaml lines 1-31

claims.text: If /health/ready also checked Redis, a Redis outage would fail readiness on every api Pod at once, leaving the Service no ready Pod, so every request through it fails although PostgreSQL is up: a slower product page becomes no api.

A fallback moves load rather than removing it: with Redis down every single-product read becomes a PostgreSQL query until Redis is back, so it is safe only while PostgreSQL can carry the extra load; otherwise the optional dependency's failure becomes the required one's.
claims.source_hint: follows from claim 7; outline item 5; backend.l3.slow-dependencies (cascading failure)

claims.text: Catching every exception and returning an empty result is not graceful degradation when the empty result is a wrong answer (e.g. an empty product list) and it hides failures from the logs.

cache-aside.sh @ stage-2 reads product 3 twice (miss, then hit), then once with the redis container stopped, then starts Redis again; it prints the status code and the number of product queries per request.
Captured output of cache-aside.sh @ stage-2: all three requests '-> 200' with product 3; queries PostgreSQL ran: 1, 0, 1 (the third with Redis stopped).
With Redis up, a product is queried again only after its copy expires (Ttl = 5 minutes, ProductCache.cs line 18) or after UpdatePriceAsync deletes it (lines 54-59).

Captured output at stage-3 with Payments stopped: POST /api/v1/orders/10/refund answers 202, the order stays 'refunding' with the request waiting in payments.refund-requests, and the refund row becomes 'refunded' once Payments is back.
